violations.line: It was also large enough to form diverse teams.

sentence_audit.sentence: In 2024, a team showed up to our hackathon with nothing but curiosity and a caffeine plan.
By dusk, they'd shipped a working prototype and won thousands of dollars.
That's how our Future of Data Hackathon team describes 2024.
If you're a student, you want a day like that.
You want to build something people will use, with someone who hires watching you work.
So the next year, we capped the student field at 40, in teams of four.
Forty was small enough that every student could get direct mentorship and meaningful access to the executives at the event.
It was also large enough to form diverse teams.
sentence_audit.issue: V1: off the core point and generic; the next sentence does not need it.

sentence_audit.sentence: Then we lined up two clients.
Beginner Track teams were set to build data and AI tools that support cancer research operations at Wood Hudson Cancer Research Laboratory in Newport, KY.
Founded in 1981, the lab maintains over 2 million tissue specimens.
Experienced Track teams were set to work with the YMCA of Greater Cincinnati on AI for member analytics, program scheduling, and outreach.
Each student would build for a client who could use the work, and get direct mentorship while doing it.
sentence_audit.issue: V2: two ideas in one sentence; the mentorship clause repeats an earlier sentence; claims_map mapping does not cover both clients.

sentence_audit.sentence: Which track would you have picked?
Read the full post: https://disruptionnow.com/blog/40-student-slots-real-world-impact
Our hackathon asked students to build AI tools for a cancer lab that holds over 2 million tissue specimens.
The lab is Wood Hudson Cancer Research Laboratory in Newport, KY.
Beginner Track teams were set to build data and AI tools that support its research operations.
Experienced Track teams were set to work with the YMCA of Greater Cincinnati on member analytics, program scheduling, and outreach.
We capped the field at 40 students, in teams of four.
That kept it small enough for every student to get direct mentorship and meaningful access to the executives at the event.
If you're a student, which track would you have picked?
